samples.summary: Third hand-maintained list of boolean inline keys instead of a shared constant. `BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS` duplicates the key enumerations already hard-coded in `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2647-2651` and `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1009` (and implicitly `inlineStylesEqual`, types.ts:404). Adding a future boolean key (e.g. smallCaps) now requires remembering three sites; the repo's reuse expectation would put one exported constant in `model/types.ts` next to `InlineStyle`/`CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE`.

The new storage invariant is enforced only at the `Doc` layer, not at the layer every write passes through, and the `DocStore` contract does not record it. `DocStore.applyStyle`/`applyStyles` (store.ts:76-97) still accept a raw `Partial<InlineStyle>` with no documented rule that `undefined` means 'remove' and `false` means 'explicit override'; `applyStyles` (used by editor.ts:1095 / text-box-editor.ts:907) bypasses `styleOffAsClear` entirely, so any future boolean write routed through the batch API silently reintroduces the dead flag the change removes. Design-fit note, not a present bug (batch is font-size-only today).
samples.evidence: store.ts:76-97 applyStyle/applyStyles doc comments make no mention of the clear-vs-false convention; only document.ts and block-helpers.ts encode it.

samples.summary: A cross-cutting data-model invariant is documented only in a feature doc. The 'a boolean turned off is cleared, not stored as false' rule governs the inline-style storage model used by the docs engine, slides text boxes and the Yorkie store, but it is filed under the font-controls feature doc (whose scope is pickers/clear-formatting) with no pointer from `docs/design/docs/docs.md` (the canonical docs data-model doc) or `docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md` (which owns the named-style cascade the exception depends on). Readers of the named-styles cascade will not find the `false`-as-override rule. A cross-reference from those docs would satisfy the 'fold into the canonical subsystem doc' expectation.
samples.evidence: docs-font-controls.md:244-283 is the only place the invariant exists; grep for 'false' in docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md returns no matches.

samples.summary: The named-style exception leaves the originating symptom unfixed inside styled blocks. In a Heading 1 (bold) or Heading 6 (italic), bold/italic toggle-off still stores an explicit `false`, so the run stays permanently split and remains pinned against a later redefinition of that named style — exactly the two consequences issue #749 describes. The issue text and the design doc do endorse the exception, so this is a scope/limitation observation rather than a violated criterion, but the invariant as written in docs-font-controls.md ('every boolean toggle-off is cleared') overstates what the code achieves for heading blocks.
samples.evidence: styleOffAsClear skips the demotion whenever `defaults[key]` is truthy (document.ts:411), and docs-font-controls.md:246-254 states the invariant with only a parenthetical exception.
